requirements.clause: **Immanence** When you Strike with the ikon, you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success.
requirements.freeText: An immanence state for this ikon that the player can turn on and off — the benefit only runs while the exemplar's spark rests in this ikon, so the sheet needs a switchable state rather than a permanent entry.

requirements.clause: you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success. This has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure.
requirements.freeText: While immanence is on, Strikes made with the weapon this ikon is imbued into crit on a natural 19, but only when that 19 would already be a success. This is an expanded critical range on YOUR OWN Strike — no lane expresses critical-range changes, so at minimum that specific Strike needs a marker carrying the rule where the player rolls it.

requirements.clause: **Transcendence—Plant Thirty Barbs** ⟨1⟩ (death, transcendence)
requirements.freeText: The character gains a named single-action activity, Plant Thirty Barbs, with the death and transcendence traits; it must appear as an action the player can find and use.

requirements.clause: **Usage** imbued into a weapon ikon that deals piercing or slashing damage
requirements.freeText: The player must designate which owned weapon this ikon is imbued into, restricted to weapons that deal piercing or slashing damage. Every later clause reads "the ikon", so the sheet cannot resolve them without that stored pick.

requirements.clause: **Immanence** When you Strike with the ikon, ...
requirements.freeText: The Immanence benefit is live only while the exemplar's divine spark is held in this ikon, so the sheet needs an on/off state per ikon (only one spark at a time) that the player flips as they shift immanence.

requirements.clause: you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success. This has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure.
requirements.freeText: An expanded critical range on Strikes with the imbued weapon — a natural 19 crits when 19 would otherwise be a success. This is not a bonus to attack, damage, or a DC, so nothing numeric can carry it; it has to print on the strike itself while the ikon's state is on.

requirements.clause: **Transcendence—Plant Thirty Barbs** ⟨1⟩ (death, transcendence)
requirements.freeText: The character gains a named 1-action activity with the death and transcendence traits. Spending it consumes the divine spark currently held in this ikon, so it is only available while that state is on and turns it off when used.

requirements.freeText: The sheet must let the player bind this record to ONE specific owned weapon (only ones dealing piercing or slashing qualify) and route everything below to that weapon's Strikes alone rather than to all Strikes. A per-record item binding — the record is inert until the player names which weapon it lives in.

requirements.clause: **Immanence** When you Strike with the ikon, you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success. This has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure.

This is a change to how the die result is read, not a modifier, so nothing in a bonus or trait field can express it.

requirements.clause: **Transcendence—Plant Thirty Barbs** ⟨1⟩ (death, transcendence)
requirements.freeText: A named one-action activity, with its action cost and its death/transcendence traits, must appear as an action the character has.

why.numbers: Three mechanical clauses: the Immanence state, the crit-range change it grants to Strikes with the imbued weapon, and a named transcendence activity. The Usage line ('imbued into a weapon ikon that deals piercing or slashing damage') is an access/usage clause, not a requirement, though the weapon it names is where the Strike marker has to land. The flavour sentence about notches carries nothing.
why.resources: An exemplar ikon makes three separate promises: it must be attached to a qualifying weapon (the Immanence text says "Strike with the ikon", so the sheet has to know which weapon that is), its Immanence benefit is live only while the divine spark rests in this ikon (an on/off state), and it teaches a 1-action Transcendence activity. The Immanence benefit itself is an expanded critical range, which is not a bonus to anything and has no numeric lane — it can only be printed on the strike it modifies.
why.unmodellable: Three mechanical clauses: a usage line that binds the record to one specific weapon, an immanence clause that changes a degree of success on Strikes with that weapon, and a named transcendence activity. The binding is included because without it neither of the other clauses has anywhere to attach — it is not a prerequisite but the anchor the effects need. The crit-on-19 clause changes the rule of the roll, not a number, so no bonus field can carry it.

requirements.clause: If the next action you take is an Athletics check to Disarm, Shove, or Trip, that action has a range of 15 feet.
requirements.freeText: The character must have this as a usable named activity on the sheet. Granting the following Disarm/Shove/Trip a 15-foot range is the activity's own resolution — the player performs it — so it needs no separate stat surface beyond the action being present with its text.

requirements.clause: You don't receive any item bonuses to that check or any circumstance bonuses related to your physical body, but if you roll a critical failure on that Athletics check, you get a failure instead.
requirements.freeText: Must be able to say that this one Athletics check drops every item bonus and any circumstance bonus that comes from your body, and that a critical failure on it becomes a failure. Both land on your OWN roll — a bonus suppression and a degree-of-success upgrade — and no lane covers either, so the printed clause has to travel with the action to where Athletics is rolled.

requirements.clause: You batter your foes with a torrent of water siphoned from your surroundings. If the next action you take is an Athletics check to Disarm, Shove, or Trip, that action has a range of 15 feet...
requirements.freeText: The character gains this as a usable named activity on the sheet, with its full text reachable — the range change, the bonus suppression, and the crit-fail-becomes-fail clause are read off that text when the player performs it.

requirements.clause: If the next action you take is an Athletics check to Disarm, Shove, or Trip, that action has a range of 15 feet.
requirements.freeText: A marker on the Disarm, Shove and Trip actions (and on Athletics) saying they are performed at a 15-foot range in this window. The reach/range at which a maneuver can be attempted is not a number the sheet totals anywhere, so it can only be printed against the actions it changes.

requirements.clause: You don't receive any item bonuses to that check or any circumstance bonuses related to your physical body
requirements.freeText: A way to SUPPRESS whole categories of bonus on a single roll: item bonuses excluded outright, and circumstance bonuses excluded selectively depending on whether their source is 'your physical body'. Every existing bonus route adds a value; there is no route that removes or filters bonuses the character already has out of one check, and the second half additionally needs bonuses tagged by whether they come from the body.

requirements.clause: but if you roll a critical failure on that Athletics check, you get a failure instead
requirements.freeText: A degree-of-success upgrade — critical failure becomes failure — scoped to one named check. It moves the outcome band, not the modifier.

why.numbers: The record is itself an activity, so its existence is the main requirement; the 15-foot range it lends to the following Athletics check is that activity's own resolution. The second sentence is separable and does touch your own roll — it suppresses two whole bonus types and upgrades a critical failure — so it is stated as its own requirement.
why.resources: This is one activity. The only thing the sheet must carry is that the character HAS it — the 15-foot range, the suppressed item/circumstance bonuses, and the critical-failure step-up are all the activity's own resolution rules, applied by the player while performing it, which the manual explicitly excludes ("the internal steps of an activity"). There is nothing to choose when taking it, nothing per-day to track, and no persistent state.
why.unmodellable: Three separate promises about the next Athletics maneuver, and two of them change rules rather than numbers. The range clause marks the Disarm/Shove/Trip actions. The bonus-exclusion clause is the unusual one: every bonus lane in the app adds; this one subtracts whole categories of bonus from a single check. The critical-failure clause is a degree-of-success shift. I did not treat 'attempt an Athletics check' as a requirement — performing the check is the player's job.

requirements.clause: You gain the undead and zombie traits
requirements.freeText: The character picks up the undead and zombie creature traits, which change what can target and affect them (undead-only effects, and everything keyed to being undead). No lane grants a creature trait to the character.

requirements.clause: and the basic undead benefits
requirements.freeText: The whole basic undead benefits package must reach the sheet: the standing immunities it confers (death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, sleep, unconscious) and void healing — void damage heals you while vitality damage harms you. The immunities have a lane; the healing reversal does not.

requirements.clause: Reduce all your Speeds by 5 feet.
requirements.freeText: A permanent -5 feet applied to every Speed the character has, not just the land Speed.

requirements.clause: While your body is deteriorated, you're Slowed 1. You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints and other weak parts of your body to recover from deterioration. You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations.
requirements.freeText: A deteriorated state the player can switch on and off, showing Slowed 1 while it is on, and cleared only by the 10-minute repair (which can ride along with daily preparations) — the text explicitly blocks removing that slowed by any other means.

requirements.clause: Your fist loses the nonlethal trait.
requirements.freeText: The character's existing fist unarmed Strike must have the nonlethal trait removed from its trait list — an edit to a strike the character already had, not a new one.

requirements.clause: You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage. Your jaws are in the brawling group and have the unarmed trait.
requirements.freeText: A new jaws unarmed Strike on the strikes list: 1d8 piercing, brawling weapon group, unarmed trait, rolled with the character's own attack bonus and damage modifiers.

requirements.clause: You can use your jaws Strike only against a creature that's grabbed or restrained by you.
requirements.freeText: The jaws Strike carries a usage restriction — legal only against a creature you have grabbed or restrained — and that restriction has to print with the strike itself, since nothing about the strike's numbers changes.

requirements.clause: You gain the undead and zombie traits
requirements.freeText: The character's creature traits must actually include undead and zombie. These gate what can target the character and, via undead, reverse healing (void heals, vitality harms). No lane in the manual covers granting a creature trait to the player character.

requirements.clause: and the basic undead benefits
requirements.freeText: The named bundle has to resolve into concrete sheet entries rather than staying as a cross-reference: the standard undead immunities (death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, unconscious) plus not needing to breathe, eat, drink, or sleep.

requirements.clause: Reduce all your Speeds by 5 feet.
requirements.freeText: A permanent -5 foot penalty applied to every Speed the character has, not only the land Speed.

requirements.clause: Your fist loses the nonlethal trait.
requirements.freeText: The already-existing fist unarmed strike must have the nonlethal trait removed — a subtraction from a strike another record granted, not a new strike.

requirements.clause: While your body is deteriorated, you're Slowed 1. ... Each day after your rest period, your body is due to natural decay. Additionally, some zombie abilities allow you to push for a greater effect in exchange for a chance of deteriorating your body.
requirements.freeText: A tracked deteriorated on/off state that the player flips: it turns itself on after each rest period and other zombie feats can turn it on, and while it is on the character is Slowed 1.

requirements.clause: You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints and other weak parts of your body to recover from deterioration. You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations.
requirements.freeText: A daily-preparation decision — spend the 10 minutes to clear the deteriorated state, or start the day slowed. The clause that nothing else can remove that slowed condition means this repair is the only thing allowed to clear the state.

requirements.clause: You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage. Your jaws are in the brawling group and have the unarmed trait.
requirements.freeText: A jaws unarmed Strike, 1d8 piercing, brawling group, unarmed trait, appearing among the character's strikes.

requirements.clause: You can use your jaws Strike only against a creature that's grabbed or restrained by you.
requirements.freeText: The granted jaws Strike carries a usage restriction that must print on it — legal only against a creature the character has grabbed or restrained.

requirements.clause: You gain the undead and zombie traits.
requirements.freeText: The character themself gains creature traits. Nothing on a character sheet holds traits that describe the PC as a creature, yet a great deal keys off them (what spells and effects can target you, what abilities have zombie/undead prerequisites). This is a property of the character, not of an item or a strike.

requirements.clause: You gain … the basic undead benefits.
requirements.freeText: 'Basic undead benefits' is a reference to a rules package, not a mechanic in itself; the sheet must expand it into its parts. The immunity portion: immune to death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison and sleep, plus no need to breathe, eat, drink, or sleep.

requirements.clause: You gain … the basic undead benefits.
requirements.freeText: The same referenced package grants darkvision.

requirements.clause: You gain … the basic undead benefits.
requirements.freeText: The same package grants negative healing — void energy restores your Hit Points and vitality energy damages you. That is an inversion of which damage type heals versus harms, a rule about the character's relationship to two energy types; nothing expresses a flipped healing polarity (it is not a resistance, an immunity, or a weakness).

requirements.clause: Reduce all your Speeds by 5 feet.
requirements.freeText: The penalty must reach EVERY Speed the character has, including fly/swim/climb/burrow gained from any other source later, not only the land Speed.

requirements.clause: Your fist loses the nonlethal trait.
requirements.freeText: A trait REMOVAL, not an addition, and it targets the universal fist unarmed attack the character was never explicitly granted. A trait list that only appends cannot express taking nonlethal away.

requirements.clause: While your body is deteriorated, you're Slowed 1. … you can't remove the slowed condition from deterioration through any other means.
requirements.freeText: A persistent 'deteriorated' state the player turns on when an ability pushes for greater effect, which applies Slowed 1 while it lasts, and which is explicitly immune to every ordinary way of removing the slowed condition. The thing to track is the state, not the condition — the condition is only its symptom.

requirements.clause: Each day after your rest period, your body is due to natural decay. … You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints and other weak parts of your body to recover from deterioration. You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations.
requirements.freeText: The deteriorated state re-arms itself every day after rest, and clearing it is a 10-minute repair that can be folded into daily preparations. This is a recurring daily upkeep step with a duration attached, not a choice among options — nothing is being picked, a state is being reset.

requirements.clause: You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage. Your jaws are in the brawling group and have the unarmed trait.
requirements.freeText: A jaws unarmed Strike with 1d8 piercing damage, the brawling weapon group, and the unarmed trait.

requirements.clause: You can use your jaws Strike only against a creature that's grabbed or restrained by you.
requirements.freeText: A legality gate riding on that one granted strike: it exists but may only be used against a creature you have grabbed or restrained. It restricts when a strike may be made at all rather than modifying any of its numbers, and it must attach to that specific strike rather than to the character.

why.numbers: Seven separate mechanical promises: two creature traits, the basic undead benefits package, a blanket Speed penalty, a deteriorated state that imposes Slowed 1 and is cleared during daily preparations, an edit to the existing fist Strike, a new jaws Strike, and a usage restriction on that jaws Strike. 'Unlike a typical zombie, you're not mindless', the decay flavour and the hunger line carry nothing.
why.resources: Seven distinct mechanical clauses: creature traits, the basic undead bundle, a speed penalty, a trait removal from the existing fist, a persistent deteriorated state, the daily-preparation repair that clears it, and a granted jaws Strike with a usage restriction. "Unlike a typical zombie, you're not mindless" and the decay flavour are not requirements.
why.unmodellable: A dense record: creature traits, a rules package referenced by name, an all-Speeds penalty, a trait REMOVAL from the baseline fist, a persistent self-state with a daily reset, a granted strike, and a restriction gating that strike. I split 'basic undead benefits' into the distinct mechanics it stands for, because a bare cross-reference shows the player nothing. 'You're not mindless' is clarifying flavour and produces nothing.

requirements.clause: once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw
requirements.freeText: A once-per-hour use the player can spend and see refresh. Spending it makes you roll a Will save twice and keep the higher — a fortune effect, not a bonus, so the Will save also needs a marker saying it is available. The use pool has a lane; the reroll itself has none.

requirements.clause: If you ever become confused, rather than attack wildly, you become stubbornly immobile, wasting all your actions until the condition ends.
requirements.freeText: The Confused condition resolves differently for this character — no wild attacks, instead immobile and losing all actions for the duration — so the marker belongs on the Confused condition itself, the same shape as a Dying-condition marker.

requirements.clause: Additionally, you emanate a nimbus of light. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light to the next 30 feet). You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action that has the concentrate trait.
requirements.freeText: A state recording whether the nimbus is currently shining, which the player can suppress and reestablish (a single concentrate action). It moves none of your own numbers — display-only — but it must be switchable because the rest of the feat is worded 'as long as your nimbus is active'.

requirements.clause: You gain the Bless Ally action.
requirements.freeText: A named action, Bless Ally, must appear on the sheet as something the character can use.

requirements.clause: once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw
requirements.freeText: A tracked use with an HOURLY period, not a daily one — one use, refreshed every hour, that the player spends.

requirements.clause: you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw
requirements.freeText: A fortune effect marked on Will saves: roll twice, keep the higher. It is not a numeric bonus, so it has to sit as a marker on the Will save with its once-per-hour cost stated.

requirements.clause: If you ever become confused, rather than attack wildly, you become stubbornly immobile, wasting all your actions until the condition ends.
requirements.freeText: The Confused condition behaves differently for this character. The replacement wording must attach to the Confused condition entry the player reads, not to any roll.

requirements.clause: you emanate a nimbus of light. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light to the next 30 feet). You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action that has the concentrate trait.
requirements.freeText: A toggle the player flips with a single concentrate action, starting on. It moves none of the character's own numbers, so a display-only state showing whether the nimbus is currently lit is all it has to be.

requirements.clause: You gain the Bless Ally action.
requirements.freeText: A named action, Bless Ally, must appear among the character's actions. Its own effect goes to an ally, so only the action's existence is owed here.

requirements.clause: once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw
requirements.freeText: A fortune effect on Will saves — roll the d20 twice and keep the higher — together with the per-hour use tracker that limits it. Rolling twice changes how the roll is made rather than what is added to it, so no bonus field expresses it; and the limit is per HOUR, a period shorter than a day.

requirements.clause: If you ever become confused, rather than attack wildly, you become stubbornly immobile, wasting all your actions until the condition ends.
requirements.freeText: A rewrite of what the Confused condition does to this specific character. It has to ride on the Confused condition entry itself (the same shape as a marker attaching to the thing it modifies), because the character's own stats are untouched — only the condition's text is.

requirements.clause: you emanate a nimbus of light. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light to the next 30 feet). You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action that has the concentrate trait.
requirements.freeText: A toggleable nimbus that changes none of the character's own numbers — a display-only running state — plus the single concentrate action that suppresses or reestablishes it. The toggle is what has to exist, since the ally benefit below is gated on whether it is currently active.

requirements.clause: You gain the Bless Ally action.
requirements.freeText: A named action must appear among the character's actions.

why.numbers: Four things land on your own sheet: an hourly fortune use on Will saves, an altered Confused condition, a suppressible nimbus, and a named action. The '+1 status bonus to saves against fear' goes to ALLIES in the emanation, not to you — Ruling F says that produces nothing on your sheet, and Ruling M has already settled that standing-inside-an-emanation is not a system to build. The bright/dim light radii are battlefield illumination, not your numbers.
why.resources: Five mechanical clauses, one of which produces nothing. The ally clause — "all allies in the area of your nimbus gain a +1 status bonus to saves against fear" — lands on someone else and is an emanation, so under Ruling F/N and Ruling M it needs no star, no modifier, and no positional model on this character's sheet; I have deliberately not listed it. The confusion clause is a rewrite of a condition's behaviour, which Ruling D places on the condition entry itself.
why.unmodellable: Four things land on the character: a fortune effect on Will saves, a rewrite of how the Confused condition behaves for them, a toggleable light emanation, and a granted action. The '+1 status bonus to saves against fear for all allies in the nimbus' clause produces NOTHING on this sheet — it lands on allies, which is settled policy; the only surface the owner allows for it is the display-only running-state mode, which the nimbus requirement already covers.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Thievery

requirements.freeText: If the character is already trained in Thievery, the feat instead becomes a free pick of any other skill to be trained in — a choice the player makes when taking the feat, and one that only appears in the already-trained case.

why.numbers: Two clauses, three requirements: the Thievery training, its already-trained fallback into a free skill choice, and the Pick a Lock success upgrade. The Access line (Mihrini ethnicity) and the childhood flavour carry nothing.
why.resources: Three clauses, one of which is an Access line and therefore not a requirement. The training clause carries its own fallback, and the Pick a Lock clause is a degree-of-success step-up rather than a bonus.
why.unmodellable: Two mechanical clauses. The proficiency grant carries its own fallback branch, which is a distinct thing to express from the grant itself. The Pick a Lock clause is the interesting one — it moves a degree of success on one skill action rather than changing any modifier. The Access line is excluded as an access clause, and the childhood-fiddling sentence is flavour.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait
requirements.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus that applies only to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait. Because the rules restrict it, it belongs as a conditional entry carrying 'against emotion effects' rather than inside the flat Will save total.

requirements.clause: when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead
requirements.freeText: A success on ANY saving throw — not just Will — against an emotion effect becomes a critical success. A degree-of-success upgrade on your own save with no lane to compute it, so it must print against the saves alongside the +1, with its wider scope made clear.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait
requirements.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus restricted to Will saves against emotion effects. Because the rules restrict it, it belongs beside the Will save with "against emotion effects" as its condition rather than inside the flat save total.

requirements.clause: and when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead
requirements.freeText: A degree-of-success step-up on ANY saving throw against an emotion effect (wider than the +1, which is Will-only): success becomes critical success. No number to add, so it has to print as a marker on the saves with its trigger.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait
requirements.freeText: A restricted +1 circumstance bonus: it belongs in the situational list with 'against effects with the emotion trait' as its condition and a star beside Will, not folded into the Will total.

requirements.clause: when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead
requirements.freeText: A degree-of-success upgrade — success becomes critical success — on ANY saving throw against an emotion effect, not just Will. It shifts the outcome band rather than the modifier, and its scope is deliberately wider than the bonus in the previous clause, so it cannot simply ride along with that entry.

why.numbers: Two clauses, and they have different scopes — the +1 is Will saves only, while the success-to-critical-success upgrade applies to ANY saving throw against an emotion effect. The vetalarana ancestry text is flavour.
why.resources: Two mechanical clauses; the vetalarana ancestry paragraph is flavour. Note the two clauses have different scopes — the bonus is Will-only, the step-up applies to any saving throw against an emotion effect — so they cannot be collapsed into one entry.
why.unmodellable: Two mechanical clauses with different scopes, which is easy to miss: the +1 is Will saves only, while the critical-success upgrade is on ANY saving throw against an emotion effect. The bonus is a restricted one, so it belongs in the situational list with its restriction rather than in the Will total. The vetalarana descent is lore.

requirements.clause: You're continuously surrounded by a Bless spell.
requirements.freeText: Your own attack rolls must carry a permanent +1 status bonus. The emanation originates on you, so you are always within it — this is the decided aura shape: a permanent star on attack rolls with the positional wording in the note. The bonus allies get is not your sheet's business.

requirements.clause: with a spell rank equal to half your level (rounded up). The radius is 15 feet, and you can't increase it.
requirements.freeText: The effect's spell rank must be shown as scaling with level (half your level rounded up). It moves no number of yours — Bless's only heightening is radius and this feat fixes the radius — so it needs printing only (it matters for counteracting).

requirements.clause: You can Dismiss the spell; if you do, it returns automatically after 1 minute.
requirements.freeText: The blessing must be switchable off and back on, so the +1 status attack bonus can be suppressed while it is dismissed.

requirements.clause: You're continuously surrounded by a Bless spell, with a spell rank equal to half your level (rounded up).
requirements.freeText: An always-on +1 status bonus to your own attack rolls, sourced from a permanently running Bless. It must reach the character's Strikes/attack rolls and be visible there with its source; the spell rank (half level, rounded up) belongs in the note since it only governs counteracting.

requirements.clause: You can Dismiss the spell; if you do, it returns automatically after 1 minute.
requirements.freeText: The player must be able to turn the running Bless off and back on — while dismissed the attack bonus is not in effect. A toggle the character owns permanently, not a per-day resource.

requirements.clause: You're continuously surrounded by a Bless spell
requirements.freeText: A permanently active, self-affecting instance of a spell the feat never restates. Because you are always at the centre of your own emanation, Bless's +1 status bonus to attack rolls applies to you unconditionally — so the sheet must carry a flat status bonus to ATTACK ROLLS whose value and type live in a different record. No lane in the vocabulary covers a flat attack-roll bonus, and none covers 'you permanently have spell X running on you' as a state rather than as a castable.

requirements.clause: with a spell rank equal to half your level (rounded up)
requirements.freeText: The rank of that continuous effect is a formula on character level (ceil(level/2)), not a fixed number. Granted-spell surfaces store a rank as a literal; this one has to be stored as a level-derived expression and re-derived every time the character levels.

requirements.clause: The radius is 15 feet, and you can't increase it
requirements.freeText: Prints the fixed 15-foot emanation, and — the mechanical part — suppresses the referenced spell's own area growth (Bless's Sustain/heightening increase). That is an override of a parameter on a record this feat itself supplies, so the note has to be attached to the granted effect rather than to the feat in isolation.

requirements.clause: You can Dismiss the spell; if you do, it returns automatically after 1 minute.
requirements.freeText: An on-by-default state the player can switch OFF, with an automatic return. The sheet needs this effect to be toggleable rather than strictly permanent — a mode whose default position is on, and whose note carries the 1-minute return.

why.numbers: Three mechanical clauses. The Bless emanation is centred on YOU, so unlike the general aura case you are always inside it — Bless gives you and allies in the area a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, so your own attack rolls carry it permanently. The ally half of Bless produces nothing on your sheet (Ruling F), and the fixed 15-foot radius is area information about that ally half, so it is not a requirement. The rank scaling changes no number of yours (Bless's heightening only widens the radius, which this feat forbids), so it is print-only. The Dismiss clause is a genuine on/off toggle.
why.resources: Three mechanical clauses. (1) A permanent Bless emanation centred on you — because you are always at the centre of your own emanation, the self-facing half is unconditional: a +1 status bonus to your attack rolls that must be expressible on the sheet's strikes/attacks. (2) The spell rank scales with level, which only matters for counteracting, so it rides along in the note rather than as its own requirement. (3) You can Dismiss it and it self-restores after 1 minute — a player-flippable on/off state. The ally-facing half of Bless (allies in the 15-foot emanation also get +1) produces nothing on this sheet under Ruling F, and the positional question is settled by Ruling M, so I did not report an aura/positional system as missing. The fixed 15-foot radius that 'can't increase' is a cap on the spell's own heightening, not a sheet surface.
why.unmodellable: Four mechanical clauses: a permanently-running spell on yourself, a level-derived rank for it, a fixed area that overrides the spell's own growth, and a dismiss/auto-return toggle. The ally half ('you and your allies in the emanation') produces nothing on this sheet under Ruling F/N, and Ruling M's positional caveat does not apply to the self-benefit because you are the origin of your own emanation and are therefore always inside it — so the self-side bonus is unconditional, not a positional star. The hard part is that the feat states no numbers at all: everything it does is defined by reference to another record (Bless).

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC ... against hazards.
requirements.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus to AC that applies only against hazards — restricted, so it sits outside the AC total with 'against hazards' as its condition.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to ... saves against hazards.
requirements.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws that applies only against hazards; all three saves are eligible since the feat names none.

requirements.clause: ...and to all of your initiative rolls.
requirements.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls, whatever statistic is being rolled for initiative (Perception, Stealth, Deception, a Lore, etc.) — it must attach to the initiative roll itself, not to one skill.

requirements.clause: If at least one of your opponents is using Deception or Diplomacy to determine their initiative, your bonus to initiative from this feat increases to +4.
requirements.freeText: An upgraded value: +4 circumstance to initiative under the stated condition, replacing the +1 entry rather than stacking with it. The trigger is enemy-side knowledge the player supplies, but the number that changes is yours.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC ... against hazards
requirements.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus to AC that applies only against hazards — restricted, so it must sit beside AC with the 'against hazards' restriction stated, not folded into the AC total.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to ... saves against hazards
requirements.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws that applies only against hazards, carried on the saves with its restriction stated.

requirements.clause: and to all of your initiative rolls
requirements.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls specifically — it must reach whatever the character rolls for initiative (Perception or a skill), not their Perception or skill checks generally.

requirements.clause: If at least one of your opponents is using Deception or Diplomacy to determine their initiative, your bonus to initiative from this feat increases to +4.
requirements.freeText: A second, larger initiative entry (+4) that replaces the +1 when an opponent rolled Deception or Diplomacy for initiative. The sheet must express the two as one upgraded entry with the printed trigger, not as two stacking bonuses.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saves against hazards
requirements.freeText: One restriction ('against hazards') covering two unrelated stat rows — AC and all three saves. The sheet must be able to mark AC and the saves from a single feat with the same `when`, rather than treating a restricted AC bonus and a restricted save bonus as unrelated entries.

requirements.clause: and to all of your initiative rolls
requirements.freeText: A bonus scoped to initiative itself, and explicitly to ALL initiative rolls. It must attach to initiative as a roll rather than to Perception, so that it still applies when initiative is rolled with Deception, Stealth or any other skill — a surface distinct from the Perception bonus row.

requirements.clause: If at least one of your opponents is using Deception or Diplomacy to determine their initiative, your bonus to initiative from this feat increases to +4.
requirements.freeText: A second value for the SAME bonus that replaces the +1 rather than stacking with it (Ruling G), gated on something only the GM knows — which statistic an opponent used to roll initiative. The sheet needs two mutually exclusive entries from one feat, or one entry whose value the player can switch, with the trigger printed in the note (Ruling H: leave it open, do not narrow it).

why.numbers: Four separate promises hide in two sentences: a restricted AC bonus, a restricted save bonus, an unrestricted initiative bonus, and an upgraded initiative bonus under a condition. Per Ruling B a flat bonus the rules restrict lives in situational with the restriction in its `when`, not in the AC/save totals; per Ruling G the +4 replaces the +1 rather than stacking with it.
why.resources: Four mechanical promises packed into two sentences, on three different sheet surfaces. The AC and saves bonuses are restricted flat bonuses, which Ruling B puts in situational with the restriction in the 'when' rather than in the stat total. Initiative gets its own entry because a bonus to one specific roll is situational, not a flat modifier. The final sentence is a genuinely separate, larger entry rather than an addition — per Ruling G an upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades, so the sheet must be able to hold both wordings and show the right one. Nothing here lands on anyone else's sheet.
why.unmodellable: Three separate promises in one paragraph, and the usual mistake here is to read it as a single +1. The first is a restricted bonus spanning two different stat rows; the second is a bonus to initiative as a ROLL (not to Perception); the third silently replaces the second with a different value under an enemy-side condition. Per Ruling B the restricted bonuses belong in situational with the restriction in their `when`, and per Ruling G the upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it.

requirements.clause: You gain a 1st-level class feat for your class.
requirements.freeText: An extra pick of one class feat of level 1 or lower, restricted to your own class's feat list, held separately from your normal class-feat slots.

requirements.clause: You gain a 1st-level class feat for your class.
requirements.freeText: The player must make and record an extra pick: one class feat of the character's own class, level 1 or lower, chosen when the feat is taken and kept with it.

requirements.clause: You gain a 1st-level class feat for your class.
requirements.freeText: A player pick constrained to class feats of the character's own class at exactly 1st level, granted outside the normal class-feat progression slots so it does not consume one.

requirements.clause: You must meet the prerequisites, but you can select the feat later in the character creation process in order to determine which prerequisites you meet.
requirements.freeText: Changes when the granted pick's prerequisites are evaluated: against the finished character, not against the build as it stood when the pick was offered. The sheet must tolerate this pick sitting unfilled, and must validate its prerequisites late without reporting the character as illegal in the interim.

why.numbers: One mechanical clause. The rest is timing/prerequisite procedure, which is not a requirement — though the pick itself must exist and be filtered to the right pool.
why.resources: One mechanical clause: the feat hands the character a class feat pick. The rest is flavour plus a character-creation sequencing allowance ('you can select the feat later ... to determine which prerequisites you meet'), which is procedural guidance about when the choice is made, not a second thing to track. Prerequisite language is excluded by instruction.
why.unmodellable: One grant plus one rules clause about when the grant is validated. The grant itself is an ordinary constrained pick. The second sentence is easy to dismiss as a prerequisites line, but it is not the feat's own prerequisite — it changes WHEN the prerequisites of the thing you pick get checked, which is a validation-timing rule.

requirements.clause: You gain a +2 status bonus to saves against diseases and poisons.
requirements.freeText: A +2 status bonus to saving throws restricted to disease and poison effects — outside the save totals, with the restriction stated.

requirements.clause: ...and to flat checks to recover from persistent poison damage.
requirements.freeText: A +2 status bonus to the flat check that ends persistent poison damage. It has no stat row of its own, so it must attach to the thing it modifies — the persistent-damage recovery check — with the value inline.

requirements.clause: if you roll a success on a save against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead.
requirements.freeText: A degree-of-success upgrade (success becomes critical success) on saves against disease and poison. Not computable by the sheet, so it must be printed alongside the same disease/poison save surface as the +2.

requirements.clause: If you have the Sacred Body class feature, when you roll a critical failure on a save against a disease or poison, you get a failure instead.
requirements.freeText: A second degree-of-success upgrade (critical failure becomes failure) on the same saves, which must appear only when the character actually has the Sacred Body class feature.

requirements.clause: You gain a +2 status bonus to saves against diseases and poisons
requirements.freeText: A +2 status bonus to saving throws restricted to disease and poison, carried beside the saves with that restriction stated rather than in the save totals.

requirements.clause: and to flat checks to recover from persistent poison damage
requirements.freeText: The same +2 must also reach the flat check made to end persistent poison damage — a marker on that recovery roll / the persistent poison condition, with the value inline and a link back to this feat.

requirements.clause: if you roll a success on a save against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead
requirements.freeText: The sheet must be able to say that this character's degree of success on disease and poison saves is upgraded one step from success to critical success — an outcome-step change on a named category of save, not a numeric modifier.

requirements.clause: If you have the Sacred Body class feature, when you roll a critical failure on a save against a disease or poison, you get a failure instead.
requirements.freeText: A second degree-of-success change on the same saves — critical failure becomes failure — that only exists if the character also has the Sacred Body class feature, so the sheet must gate it on possessing that feature.

requirements.clause: You gain a +2 status bonus to saves against diseases and poisons
requirements.freeText: A restricted save bonus keyed to the SOURCE of the save (disease or poison) rather than to a save row, applying across Fortitude, Reflex and Will alike.

requirements.clause: and to flat checks to recover from persistent poison damage
requirements.freeText: A flat check is not a statistic on the sheet, so there is no row to bonus. Per Ruling D the +2 has to hang on the thing it modifies — the persistent poison damage condition and its recovery roll — which means the sheet needs a marker attachable to a condition's own check, with the value inline, not a bonus on any stat.

requirements.clause: In addition, if you roll a success on a save against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead.
requirements.freeText: A degree-of-success upgrade. It changes the result table for a whole class of saves and moves no number at all, so no bonus lane can express it. The sheet needs a per-check outcome-shift field carrying which check it applies to, which trigger scopes it (disease or poison), which degree is affected, and which direction it moves.

requirements.clause: If you have the Sacred Body class feature, when you roll a critical failure on a save against a disease or poison, you get a failure instead.
requirements.freeText: A SECOND, independent outcome shift (critical failure to failure) that exists only when the character owns another named record. Two things are needed: the same outcome-shift expression as above, and a way for one clause of a feat to be gated on possessing a specific class feature so the upgraded result appears only for characters who have it.

why.numbers: Five clauses; one of them is dead on arrival. The +2 to saves and the +2 to the persistent-poison flat check are two different surfaces. The allies-in-your-aura clause lands on someone else's sheet and therefore produces nothing here (Ruling F) — do not read its absence as a gap. The two degree-of-success upgrades change no computed number but must be printed where the roll is made; the second is additionally gated on owning the Sacred Body class feature.
why.resources: Five clauses; the middle one is an ally clause and produces nothing. (1) and (2) are restricted status bonuses on two different surfaces — the saves themselves, and the flat check to recover from persistent poison, which under Ruling D marks the persistent-damage recovery roll rather than inventing a flat-check stat row. (3) 'Allies in your champion's aura get this benefit ... +1' lands on other people's sheets — Ruling F says nothing on yours, and Ruling M settles the aura question, so I report no requirement for it. (4) and (5) are degree-of-success adjustments (success becomes critical success; with Sacred Body, critical failure becomes failure). No lane in the manual covers shifting a save's degree of success, and the DECIDED SCOPE section does not rule it out, so I state them in free text rather than forcing them into 'note'.
why.unmodellable: Five clauses, and only the first is an ordinary bonus. The ally sentence ('Allies in your champion's aura get this benefit, but their bonus is +1') produces NOTHING on this sheet — Ruling F/N plus Ruling M settle it, and the parenthetical '(Your allies don't share this benefit.)' is likewise ally-side. The flat-check clause has no stat row and falls to Ruling D. The two remaining clauses change the degree-of-success table rather than any number, which is the shape nothing in the vocabulary reaches.

requirements.clause: You have familiarity with weapons with the jotunborn trait plus the bola, greataxe, halberd, maul, longspear, and war flail—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
requirements.freeText: Your weapon proficiency for a specific named set — every weapon with the jotunborn trait, plus bola, greataxe, halberd, maul, longspear and war flail — must be computed one category down: martial ones use your simple-weapon rank, advanced ones use your martial rank. This changes the attack bonus shown for those weapons; it grants no rank increase of its own.

requirements.clause: You have familiarity with weapons with the jotunborn trait plus the bola, greataxe, halberd, maul, longspear, and war flail—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
requirements.freeText: For a specific weapon set — everything with the jotunborn trait, plus bola, greataxe, halberd, maul, longspear and war flail — the sheet must compute proficiency one category down: martial ones use the character's simple-weapon proficiency, advanced ones use their martial proficiency. It must follow the character's proficiency as it changes with level, not bake in a fixed rank.

requirements.clause: You have familiarity with weapons with the jotunborn trait plus the bola, greataxe, halberd, maul, longspear, and war flail—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
requirements.freeText: Not a proficiency rank and not a bonus: a per-weapon CATEGORY override (martial read as simple, advanced read as martial) applied only when that weapon's proficiency is resolved, leaving the weapon martial/advanced for every other purpose. The affected set is defined two ways at once — dynamically by a trait (any weapon carrying the jotunborn trait, including ones that gain it later) and by an explicit six-name list — so the sheet needs trait-driven set membership unioned with a name list, feeding a downgrade rule at strike-proficiency lookup time.

why.numbers: Two clauses, one of which is an access clause and so not a requirement (though it does decide what appears in pickers). The familiarity clause is the mechanical one: it shifts the proficiency category used for a named set of weapons, which changes your attack modifier with them.
why.resources: One clause that must reach the sheet. The proficiency clause names a weapon set by trait (jotunborn) plus six named weapons, and remaps each one's category downward — martial counts as simple, advanced counts as martial — so the character's Strikes with those weapons must be built off the lower category's proficiency rank as it advances. The opening sentence is an access grant for uncommon weapons; access clauses are excluded by instruction, so I did not report it. Nothing here is a rank increase, a bonus, or a new action.
why.unmodellable: Two clauses. The first is an access clause (uncommon weapons with the jotunborn trait) and is excluded by the not-requirements list. The second is the mechanical one, and it is not a proficiency rank — it rewrites the CATEGORY a weapon is looked up under, for one specific set of weapons, where that set is defined by a trait and by name simultaneously.

requirements.clause: You gain the Untrained Improvisation general feat.
requirements.freeText: The named general feat Untrained Improvisation must be added to the character for free, with everything it in turn grants.

requirements.clause: you can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained, even if you are untrained.
requirements.freeText: The trained-proficiency gate on skill actions is lifted for this character: any skill action listed as requiring trained must still be reachable and shown as attemptable while untrained. No number changes, but the availability statement must be visible.

requirements.clause: You gain the Untrained Improvisation general feat.
requirements.freeText: The character receives the named general feat Untrained Improvisation without spending a feat slot; it must appear among their feats.

requirements.clause: you can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained, even if you are untrained
requirements.freeText: A permanent permission flag: skill actions that carry a trained-proficiency requirement must remain available to this character at untrained, so the sheet must not treat 'requires trained' as a bar for them.

requirements.clause: You gain the Untrained Improvisation general feat.
requirements.freeText: A specific named general feat is added to the character, bringing whatever that feat itself carries.

requirements.clause: In addition, you can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained, even if you are untrained.
requirements.freeText: A global rules waiver with no number in it: it strips the trained-or-better requirement from every skill action that carries one. The sheet needs a character-level flag that changes action AVAILABILITY — trained-only skill actions must stop being filtered out or greyed out for this character — which no bonus lane can carry. A printed note is the floor; the actual requirement is that the gate itself is suppressed.

why.numbers: Two clauses. The first is a straightforward named-feat grant (whatever Untrained Improvisation itself does is that record's requirement, not this one's). The second changes no number but lifts a gate: trained-only skill actions become attemptable while untrained, so the sheet must not present them as unavailable.
why.resources: Two clauses. The first is a named feat grant, which the player must receive (Untrained Improvisation's own benefit lives on that record, not here). The second is a standing permission that changes what the character may attempt: trained-only skill actions become available while untrained. That is an exception to a general rule rather than a restatement of one, and it is not a bonus, so no lane in the manual covers it — I state it plainly instead.
why.unmodellable: Two clauses. The first is a plain named grant. The second is the interesting one: it is not a bonus but a blanket waiver of a gate, which changes which actions are legal for the character rather than changing any number.

why.numbers: The feat has exactly one mechanical clause: 'that foe is off-guard to you for 1 round'. The entire effect lands on the ENEMY's condition, and off-guard is named verbatim in the DECIDED SCOPE section as something that produces nothing on your sheet. The trigger clause (a larger foe crit-hits and damages you) is a trigger, not a requirement. No number or value on your own sheet changes: not your attack, not your AC, not a save. Nothing required.
why.resources: The feat has exactly one mechanical clause: when a larger foe critically hits and damages you, that foe becomes off-guard to you for 1 round. Every part of that lands on the ENEMY — the condition is applied to the foe, and off-guard is a reduction to the target's AC. DECIDED SCOPE names this case explicitly ('off-guard, forced movement, the target's AC or cover — none is a requirement'). The trigger line is not a requirement either. Nothing is chosen, tracked, spent, toggled, or gained; no number on the character's own sheet ever moves.
why.unmodellable: The text splits into exactly two clauses: a trigger (a larger foe critically hits and damages you) and its effect (that foe is off-guard to you for 1 round). Trigger lines are excluded outright. The effect lands entirely on the ENEMY — off-guard is a condition on the foe, and its cash value is a penalty to the target's AC, which is target-side. DECIDED SCOPE (Ruling F/N: 'target-side numbers the app does not model — the target's AC, cover — get no surface either', plus the standing 'effects on enemies or the battlefield' exclusion) settles this as producing nothing on your sheet: no star, no modifier, no note. There is no action to grant, no state to toggle, no per-day resource, and no number of your own that moves.

requirements.clause: When you use Lore to Earn Income, if you roll a critical failure, you instead get a failure.
requirements.freeText: A conditional marker on the Lore skill entry (per Ruling C, on every Lore skill that could perform Earn Income) reading that a critical failure on an Earn Income check becomes a failure. Note that this is a degree-of-success adjustment, not a numeric bonus — no lane computes degrees of success, so what the sheet must be able to express is the conditional marker with the Earn Income trigger in its 'when', per Ruling D (the mark attaches to the action it modifies).

requirements.clause: If you're an expert in Lore, you gain twice as much income from a failed check to Earn Income, unless it was originally a critical failure.
requirements.freeText: A printable clause, gated on holding expert rank in Lore, that doubles the income from a failed Earn Income check (excluding an original critical failure). Nothing on the sheet computes downtime income, so the requirement is that the clause can be carried and shown conditionally against the Lore/Earn Income entry rather than that a number be recalculated.

requirements.clause: When you use Lore to Earn Income, if you roll a critical failure, you instead get a failure.
requirements.freeText: A marker on the Earn Income activity / on the character's Lore skills recording that a critical failure on this specific use becomes a failure. It is a degree-of-success change, not a bonus, so there is no number to add — the sheet only has to print it where the player looks when performing Earn Income with Lore (per Ruling D the mark attaches to the action, and per Ruling C every Lore skill that could perform it).

requirements.clause: If you're an expert in Lore, you gain twice as much income from a failed check to Earn Income, unless it was originally a critical failure.
requirements.freeText: A second marker on the same Earn Income / Lore surface that only appears once the character's Lore proficiency reaches expert, stating that income from a failed check is doubled (excluding a result that was originally a critical failure). The gate is a proficiency-rank check on the specific Lore skill being used, and the payload is a downtime currency amount rather than a roll modifier.

requirements.clause: When you use Lore to Earn Income, if you roll a critical failure, you instead get a failure.
requirements.freeText: A degree-of-success reclassification bound to one activity and one skill family: a critical failure on a Lore check made to Earn Income is read as a failure instead. Nothing numeric changes — the result STEP of the roll is rewritten. It must attach to Earn Income under every Lore skill the character has (Ruling C's star-every-skill-that-could-perform-the-action shape), and it is not a bonus, so situational/passiveEffects cannot carry it.

requirements.clause: If you're an expert in Lore, you gain twice as much income from a failed check to Earn Income, unless it was originally a critical failure.
requirements.freeText: The Earn Income activity must be able to carry a rider that is gated on a proficiency RANK (expert in Lore), that multiplies the activity's payout on one specific degree of success (failure), and that carves out an exception for a failure which only became a failure via the previous clause — i.e. the rider has to know the roll's ORIGINAL degree, not just its final one. Ruling D settles where such a marker sits (on the action it modifies), but the sheet holds no income figure to double and no rank-gated marker text.

why.numbers: Two distinct mechanical clauses. Both are conditional riders on Lore's Earn Income use rather than flat bonuses, so per the doc's 'NOT lanes' note a bonus to one specific use is situational, never skillTrained. The second clause has its own precondition (expert in Lore) and its own exclusion (not if originally a critical failure), so it is a separate requirement, not a restatement of the first. The opening sentence is flavour.
why.resources: Two separate promises: a degree-of-success upgrade on one activity, and a rank-gated doubling of the money that activity yields. Neither is a stat bonus and neither costs a resource, so nothing is spent or tracked — but both must be visible on the Earn Income/Lore surface, and the second must switch on by itself when Lore reaches expert. The opening sentence is flavour.
why.unmodellable: Sentence one is flavour. The two mechanical clauses are both rules-changes on the Earn Income downtime activity rather than numbers: one rewrites a degree of success, the other multiplies a payout and is gated both on proficiency rank and on which degree of success was originally rolled. Neither is a bonus, so no lane in sections A–J fits; the DECIDED SCOPE section does not settle downtime income, and Ruling D only fixes the surface (a marker on the action), not the expressible content.

requirements.clause: You become trained in your choice of Deception or Thievery
requirements.freeText: A player pick that grants the trained proficiency rank, with the pool restricted to exactly two named skills (Deception, Thievery) rather than any skill.

requirements.clause: if you are already trained in both, you become an expert in one instead
requirements.freeText: The already-trained fallback here does not redirect to a different skill: it must be able to yield the EXPERT rank in one of those same two skills, chosen by the player. So the sheet must express a conditional rank upgrade (trained -> expert) in Deception or Thievery that fires only when both are already trained.

requirements.clause: choose a single, discrete urban or wilderness location, such as "Mzali" or "the Verduran Forest"; this becomes your favored location ... You can change your favored location by spending 1 week of downtime
requirements.freeText: The sheet must record and display a player-authored favored location. Unlike a normal choice this has no enumerable option list — it is a free-text value the player types, and it must remain editable later (the feat allows changing it).

requirements.clause: When you are in this location and undetected by all enemies, you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than half your Speed.
requirements.freeText: A conditional marker on Stealth / the Sneak action stating that no Stealth check is rolled at all, gated on three printed conditions: being in your recorded favored location, being undetected by all enemies, and moving no more than half your Speed. It carries no number — the value it replaces is the roll itself. Whether you are standing in your favored location is unknowable to the sheet, so per Ruling M's shape the condition belongs in the marker's note rather than being modelled.

requirements.clause: You become trained in your choice of Deception or Thievery.
requirements.freeText: A choice the player makes when taking the feat, from a fixed two-option list (Deception, Thievery), granting the trained rank in the picked skill.

requirements.clause: if you are already trained in both, you become an expert in one instead
requirements.freeText: Nearest lane, but the shape differs from the usual fallback: this does not redirect the player to a different skill, it converts the grant into a RANK UPGRADE to expert, and the player still picks which of Deception or Thievery is upgraded. So the sheet must detect that both skills are already trained, then offer the same two-option pick with a different payload (expert instead of trained).

requirements.clause: When you take this dedication, choose a single, discrete urban or wilderness location, such as "Mzali" or "the Verduran Forest"; this becomes your favored location. … You can change your favored location by spending 1 week of downtime in the new location.
requirements.freeText: No lane fits. The sheet must store a player-AUTHORED free-text value — the name of a favored location — captured when the feat is taken and editable afterwards. It is not a pick from an enumerable option list, so the standard choice lane's option-set shape does not describe it; there is no correct answer for the app to offer, only a text field the player fills in. The stored value is load-bearing because the feat's remaining clauses are gated on being in that named place.

requirements.clause: When you are in this location and undetected by all enemies, you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than half your Speed.
requirements.freeText: A marker on Stealth / the Sneak action carrying the full condition in its 'when': you are in your recorded favored location, undetected by all enemies, and moving no more than half your Speed. The payload is 'no check is rolled at all', which is not a bonus value — the sheet only has to print the licence beside Sneak.

requirements.clause: During exploration, this also allows you to automatically approach within 15 feet of other creatures while Avoiding their Notice, as long as they aren't actively Searching or on guard.
requirements.freeText: A second marker on the Avoid Notice activity (and the Stealth skill) with its own condition — in the favored location, targets not Searching and not on guard — stating the approach to 15 feet succeeds automatically. Distinct from the Sneak clause above: different action, different condition, so under the stacking ruling it is shown as its own entry rather than merged.

requirements.clause: You become trained in your choice of Deception or Thievery
requirements.freeText: A player pick between two specifically named skills, granting trained proficiency in the chosen one.

requirements.clause: if you are already trained in both, you become an expert in one instead
requirements.freeText: The redundancy branch is not 'pick a different skill' — its payload differs in KIND from the main grant: a rank upgrade to expert in one of the same two skills, still a player choice. The sheet must express a fallback that changes what is granted (trained-in-a-choice becomes expert-in-a-choice), not merely which target receives it.

requirements.clause: choose a single, discrete urban or wilderness location, such as "Mzali" or "the Verduran Forest"; this becomes your favored location. … You can change your favored location by spending 1 week of downtime in the new location
requirements.freeText: A free-text, player-typed value stored on the character (the favored location) which the feat's own later clauses refer back to, and which must remain editable afterwards. requirements.clause: When you are in this location and undetected by all enemies, you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than half your Speed.

why.numbers: Four sheet-side clauses. why.resources: Five distinct promises. why.unmodellable: Six clauses. (1) trained in Deception or Thievery — skillChoice. (2) the already-trained-in-both branch — redundantFallback, but with an upgrade payload. requirements.clause: Once per day, you can cast 7th-rank Dragon Form as an innate arcane spell, transforming into a cloud dragon.
requirements.freeText: Dragon Form must appear as a once-per-day innate spell of the arcane tradition, cast at rank 7, with its per-day use tracked. The text grants no spell attack or spell DC proficiency, so nothing else about spellcasting changes.

requirements.clause: The spell automatically heightens to 8th level if you're 16th level and 9th rank if you're 18th level.

The resource being reset is not the character's — it exists only inside a temporary polymorph form granted by a spell — so the sheet needs a use counter that lives on a form, and a rule that refills it off a die result.

why.numbers: Five sheet-side clauses. The heightening line is separated from the casting line because it makes the spell rank a level-derived value rather than a constant, which is a different thing to express. The form's strikes and the form state are separated because one is a set of attack rows with exact dice and traits and the other is the toggleable state that scopes them. The closing 'Special' line (this feat counts as Shape of the Dragon for feat requirements) is prerequisite bookkeeping and is excluded per the task's own list.
why.resources: Five clauses. The per-day innate spell is the resource to spend; the rank silently rescales at levels 16 and 18; and the remainder is a feat-specific battle-form statblock — cloud walk, a breath weapon, and four differently-shaped strikes — all of which exist only while transformed and therefore need a turn-on/turn-off state to live in. The 'Special' line about substituting for Shape of the Dragon is a prerequisite clause and requires nothing.
why.unmodellable: The densest of the six. Clauses: the innate casting itself; its automatic level-indexed heightening; a crit-triggered recharge of a form-owned resource; the 'while in this form' wrapper that gates everything after it; four strikes with their own dice and traits; a Breath Weapon action; cloud walk as a terrain permission; and the Special equivalence line. The rules-shaped ones with no lane are the recharge-on-crit (resetting a limit that belongs to a temporary form), cloud walk (permission rather than speed), and the prerequisite alias. Nothing here lands on an ally, an enemy, or a companion, so DECIDED SCOPE removes none of it.

why.numbers: Three clauses. The skill grant is really two — a two-option pick, plus an escalation to expert when the pick is already trained. Per Ruling B a restricted flat bonus is situational with the restriction in its `when`, not a flat save bonus. The aura's emotion/mental/visual traits and its radius affect only other creatures and the GM, so they carry no requirement.
why.resources: Two mechanical clauses: a skill pick with a trained-or-expert outcome, and a permanent aura. The skill grant is a two-option choice, and its rank is not fixed — it escalates to expert if the chosen skill was already trained, which is a redundancy rule the manual's redundantFallback (choose a different skill) does not describe. The aura's fear bonus does land on the character themself as well as allies, so it is a real self-facing bonus; the ally half produces nothing per Ruling F/N, and the shape of the self half is settled by Ruling M (permanent star, positional condition in the note) — settled, but still a requirement that the star exist.

requirements.freeText: The chosen spells are added to the character's spell list so they become eligible when adding or swapping repertoire spells — they are not learned outright.

requirements.clause: Special You can select this feat more than once. You can't choose the same spells more than once, but you can choose a different domain or a different deity with the same domain you've previously selected with this feat.
requirements.freeText: The feat is repeatable, each taking stores its own deity and its own up-to-three spell picks, and the later takings' option lists must exclude spells already chosen by an earlier taking while still permitting the same domain via a different deity. Requires per-instance choice storage plus cross-instance exclusion.

why.numbers: Two live clauses plus a repeatability rule. The pick is nested — a deity constrained by your mystery's domains, then up to three of that deity's cleric spells — and the result is an addition to your own spell list, which is a sheet-side change to what you may legally take into your repertoire. The 'you can select from these when you add or swap' sentence is just the consequence of the list addition, not a second requirement, and the Source line is bibliography.
why.resources: Two picks and one list change: choose a qualifying deity, then choose up to three of that deity's cleric spells to add to your spell list, plus the Special clause making the feat repeatable with independent picks each time. The opening sentence is flavour and the repertoire sentence just states where the added spells can then be selected.
why.unmodellable: Three clauses. The deity pick is a choice whose option list must be computed from another feature the character already has (the mystery's granted domains), and the spell pick is a second choice nested inside the first (that deity's cleric spells). The Special line is genuinely mechanical here, not a frequency line: it makes the feat repeatable with per-instance state and forbids repeating earlier picks.

requirements.clause: You have familiarity with martial crossbows and firearms, treating them as simple weapons for the purposes of proficiency.

why.numbers: Five mechanical clauses; the usual stopping point is the weapon familiarity. The class DC clause is the interesting one — a non-gunslinger gains a trained rank in the gunslinger class DC, and no lane in the manual covers class DC at all (the proficiency lanes name weapons, armour, saves, Perception and spell attacks/DCs only). The way pick is a choice whose only mechanical output is a skill, with an explicit redundancy fallback. The uncommon-access sentence is an access clause and carries no requirement.
why.resources: Four mechanical clauses: weapon familiarity, a class DC proficiency, a way pick, and a skill grant determined by that pick with an already-trained fallback. The uncommon-item clause is an access clause, and 'you don't gain any other abilities from your choice of way' is a clarification — neither is a requirement.
why.unmodellable: Five mechanical clauses plus one access clause I excluded. Two of them are shape-changing rather than number-changing: weapon familiarity remaps a weapon CATEGORY for proficiency purposes instead of granting a rank, and the class DC is a whole statistic (with its own attribute) that an archetype character otherwise does not possess — the manual's proficiency lanes name weapons, armour, saves, Perception and spells, but no class DC. The 'no other abilities' sentence is a real storage constraint: the way must be recorded as an identity without its normal grants.

requirements.clause: Once per hour, you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape.

requirements.freeText: One use per hour, with the hour counted from when the form ends rather than when it starts — a per-hour resource with a cooldown, not a per-day pool.

requirements.freeText: Print beside the form: the form is restricted to the character's own inherent animal, and no fly Speed is gained even when that animal flies. The denial is explicit, so the state must not add a fly Speed.

requirements.clause: …you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape.
requirements.freeText: The Change Shape action the character already has gains an additional named form to enter — critter shape — so the option must appear on the existing action rather than as a standalone activity.

requirements.clause: Once per hour… You can remain in critter shape for up to 10 minutes, after which you transform back… and can't enter your critter shape again for 1 hour.
requirements.freeText: A per-hour resource the player spends: one entry per hour, a 10-minute cap on how long the shape lasts, and a 1-hour lockout before it can be entered again.

requirements.clause: While in critter shape, you gain the effect of a 1st-rank Pest Form, except you can only transform into an animal matching your inherent animal.
requirements.freeText: A state the player turns on and off that, while active, applies 1st-rank Pest Form's real sheet numbers (Tiny size and the form's stat profile) and no fly Speed, with the form restricted to the character's inherent animal.

requirements.clause: you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape
requirements.freeText: Adds a new shape option to the Change Shape action the character was already granted elsewhere, rather than teaching a standalone action.

requirements.clause: Once per hour, you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape.
requirements.freeText: A once-per-hour resource — an hourly period rather than the usual per-day one.

requirements.clause: While in critter shape, you gain the effect of a 1st-rank Pest Form
requirements.freeText: A toggleable battle-form state whose entire content is 'the effect of ⟨named spell⟩ at ⟨rank N⟩'. The sheet must be able to resolve a granted state by reference to another record's stat block — the form's replacement AC, size, Speeds, senses and skill modifiers, and the battle-form rules that override the character's own statistics — for a spell that is neither known nor cast.

requirements.clause: except you can only transform into an animal matching your inherent animal
requirements.freeText: The form list is narrowed to a single animal determined by an earlier heritage selection (the character's inherent animal), so the state's options depend on another stored pick.

requirements.clause: You can remain in critter shape for up to 10 minutes, after which you transform back into your hybrid shape and can't enter your critter shape again for 1 hour.
requirements.freeText: The state carries a maximum duration (10 minutes) that ends it automatically, and the 1-hour lockout is measured from when the state ends rather than from when it began — a cooldown anchored to the end of a mode, not a use counted at its start.

requirements.clause: If your inherent animal has a fly Speed, you can turn into that animal (unlike normal for 1st-rank pest form), but you still don't gain a fly Speed.
requirements.freeText: An explicit override of the referenced spell's own restriction, plus an explicit denial: the form must not confer a fly Speed even though the chosen animal has one.

why.numbers: Four clauses. The feat does not teach a new action — it adds an option to the Change Shape action the character already has, which is a different shape from granting one. The transformed state is a real toggleable state that replaces the character's own numbers with a battle form's for up to 10 minutes, and it carries a size change. The frequency is per-hour with a cooldown, not per-day. The last sentence is an explicit denial (no fly Speed) plus a form restriction, worth printing but not computable. The 'smaller, younger version' line is appearance only.
why.resources: Three mechanical clauses: a new option on the already-granted Change Shape action, a once-per-hour resource with a 10-minute duration and a 1-hour lockout, and the transformed state itself. Returning to hybrid shape is an internal step of the activity; the 'smaller, younger version' and 'you still don't gain a fly Speed' clauses change no sheet value.
why.unmodellable: The feat has no numbers of its own — its entire effect is 'you gain the effect of a named spell at a named rank', which means the sheet must be able to express a granted battle form defined by reference to a spell the character neither knows nor casts. Around that sit a use limit, a maximum duration whose expiry starts a cooldown, a form list narrowed by an earlier heritage pick, and an explicit carve-out that the form still grants no fly Speed. The 'transform back at any time' sentence is the internal operation of the action and needs nothing.

requirements.clause: You gain resistance equal to your level to damage dealt by swarms, troops, and creatures who occupy the same space as you.

requirements.clause: You gain resistance equal to your level to damage dealt by swarms, troops, and creatures who occupy the same space as you.
