requirements.clause: You gain the Overawe Crowd activity.

why.resources: Two mechanical clauses: a level-scaling restricted resistance and a granted activity. The first and third sentences are flavour.
why.unmodellable: Two clauses. The resistance is unusual on both axes: its value is the character's level rather than a printed number, so it must recompute on level-up, and it is keyed to WHO is dealing the damage (swarms, troops, creatures sharing your space) rather than to a damage type. requirements.clause: Reroll the failed save and use the new result.

Nothing about the save's total changes; what the sheet needs is a place on the Reflex save to hang "once per day, if you fail, reroll and use the new result" (a forced-reroll / fortune effect), together with the once-per-day use so the player can see whether it is still available, and the "you can see the night sky" condition printed alongside it. No lane covers rerolling a roll: `situational` and `note` both assume a bonus or a printed remark, and this is neither.

why.numbers: The Frequency, Trigger and Requirements lines are excluded by the brief. What remains is (a) the feat is itself a reaction, so the sheet must carry it as one rather than as a passive, and (b) the effect is a reroll of a failed Reflex save — no number on the sheet changes, so under Ruling D the surface is a marker on the thing it modifies, the Reflex save. Nothing here touches an ally, an enemy or an aura.
why.resources: Three of the four lines are excluded by policy: the Trigger line, the Requirements line ('you can see the night sky' is GM-adjudicated positioning/visibility), and the reroll itself, which is dice the player rolls rather than a number on the sheet. What survives is the resource: this is a once-per-day ability, so the sheet must count it. The Frequency header is metadata rather than its own mechanical clause, but the thing it caps is a per-day resource the player spends, which is squarely what must be tracked.
why.unmodellable: Frequency, Trigger and Requirements lines are excluded by policy, and the flavour sentence about the stars is not mechanical. That leaves exactly one mechanical clause — the reroll — which is a rules change attached to a specific save and has no lane.

requirements.clause: You gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed, using your wings to stay aloft.

requirements.clause: You gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed, using your wings to stay aloft.

why.resources: One mechanical clause. Nothing is chosen or spent; the whole feat is a new movement type. The load-bearing detail is that the value is derived rather than fixed.
why.unmodellable: One mechanical clause. The only thing worth calling out beyond the plain `speed` lane is that the value is derived rather than fixed. "Using your wings to stay aloft" is flavour.

requirements.freeText: The override is gated on the character's proficiency rank in whichever skill performs the action: it applies only for skills the character is master or better in. The marker's condition therefore has to be evaluated per-skill against current rank (and per Ruling C, the plausible performing skills are Arcana/Nature/Occultism/Religion), not stated as a flat always-on property.

why.numbers: Splitting the text: (a) 'Once per round' is a frequency line — excluded by the brief. (b) The one real mechanical clause changes the ACTION COST of an already-existing general skill action (Recognize a Spell) from its printed cost to a free action, gated on the skill used being master rank. No number on the sheet moves, so per Ruling D the surface attaches to the thing it modifies — the Recognize a Spell action — rather than to any stat row. The feat does not teach a new activity, so this is not grantsAction.
why.resources: One mechanical clause. The feat teaches no new action — Recognize a Spell already exists — it only changes that action's cost to a free action, once per round, and only when the skill used is one you're master in. Per Ruling D the marker attaches to the thing it modifies (the action), and per Ruling C to every skill that could perform it. 'Once per round' is not a per-day resource, so it belongs in the marker's wording rather than a use counter.
why.unmodellable: Two mechanical clauses hide behind one sentence: (a) Recognize a Spell's ACTION COST is replaced with a free action, and (b) only when the skill used is one you're a master in. Nothing is granted and no number moves — the sheet has to carry an altered cost on an action it did not grant. Ruling D settles the surface (the marker attaches to the thing it modifies, i.e. the Recognize a Spell action, value inline), so this is a marker requirement, not a missing positional/enemy system. 'Once per round' is a frequency line and is therefore not itself a requirement, but it is part of what the marker must print. 'You Recognize Spells swiftly' is flavour.

requirements.clause: Choose holy or unholy.
requirements.freeText: A two-option pick recorded on the character, made once. The stored answer must feed the damage rider below, because it sets both the trait attached to the extra damage and the opposing trait that gates it.

requirements.clause: While you are taking persistent bleed damage, you can Interact to coat a piercing or slashing weapon you're wielding with your blood. Until the end of your turn...
requirements.freeText: A toggleable state the player turns on for a single weapon and that runs until the end of the turn, so the strike rider below is live only while it is on. The printed precondition (you are taking persistent bleed damage, or you paid the self-damage instead) belongs in the mode's note.

requirements.clause: ...your Strikes with that weapon deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage with the chosen trait to creatures with the opposing trait.
requirements.freeText: While the state is on, Strikes with the coated weapon add 1d6 spirit damage carrying the chosen holy/unholy trait. Two conditions must be expressible: the rider is scoped to that one wielded piercing or slashing weapon, and it only lands against creatures with the trait opposing the one chosen.

requirements.clause: Choose holy or unholy.
requirements.freeText: The player picks holy or unholy when taking the feat, and the sheet must remember that pick, because it decides the trait on the damage the feat later adds and which creatures the damage applies against.

requirements.clause: Until the end of your turn, your Strikes with that weapon deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage with the chosen trait to creatures with the opposing trait.
requirements.freeText: The player must be able to turn on a temporary state (switched on by the Interact that coats the weapon, lasting to the end of the turn) that adds 1d6 spirit damage carrying the chosen holy or unholy trait to Strikes with the one piercing or slashing weapon being wielded — with the restriction that it only lands on creatures of the opposing trait carried in its wording. The extra die is a rider on that weapon's Strike damage, not a flat bonus, and the damage trait must follow the holy/unholy pick.

requirements.clause: Choose holy or unholy.
requirements.freeText: A one-time recorded pick of holy or unholy. It is load-bearing, not cosmetic: it sets the trait carried by the extra damage and defines which creatures ('the opposing trait') the rider fires against.

requirements.clause: While you are taking persistent bleed damage, you can Interact to coat a piercing or slashing weapon you're wielding with your blood. Until the end of your turn ...
requirements.freeText: A toggleable state whose duration is until the end of the current turn, whose availability is gated on the character currently taking persistent bleed damage (or on paying the self-damage alternative), and which is further gated on wielding a piercing or slashing weapon.

requirements.clause: your Strikes with that weapon deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage with the chosen trait to creatures with the opposing trait
requirements.freeText: An extra 1d6 damage die of type spirit added to Strikes, carrying the holy or unholy trait taken from the earlier pick, and applying only against targets bearing the opposing trait — so the rider must be expressible as conditional bonus damage rather than a flat damage increase.

requirements.clause: coat a piercing or slashing weapon you're wielding ... Strikes with that weapon
requirements.freeText: No lane covers this shape: the rider must bind to ONE specific wielded weapon instance chosen at the moment the state is switched on — not to a weapon group, trait, or every Strike — and that binding lasts only for the turn. The sheet needs a way for an activated state to name which inventory weapon it is riding on.

why.numbers: Three mechanical clauses plus one that is not a requirement. (1) A binary player choice of holy or unholy, made once when the feat is taken — the pick decides both the damage trait and which creatures the extra damage applies to, so each option grants something different (effectChoices[].grant shape). (2) A state you switch on with an Interact and that lapses at end of turn — that is the mode lane; the Interact's internal steps are not requirements, only the ability to turn the state on. (3) While that state is on, Strikes with the coated weapon gain an extra damage die — a weapon damage rider, doubly conditional (that specific wielded piercing/slashing weapon, and only against creatures with the trait opposing the one chosen). The 'deal 1d6 damage to yourself' alternative is a cost paid in HP; per Ruling E, HP and damage never move sheet stats, so it produces no requirement.
why.resources: Three mechanical clauses: a permanent pick made when the feat is taken, a turn-long toggled damage rider on a wielded weapon, and an alternative that costs the character HP. The self-damage alternative produces no requirement — HP and damage never move sheet stats (Ruling E).
why.unmodellable: Four separate promises: a permanent build-time pick (holy/unholy), a turn-length activated state, a damage rider that is doubly conditional (bound to one particular weapon AND only against opposing-trait targets), and an alternative self-damage cost. The self-damage — including 'can't be resisted in any way' — is settled by Ruling E: HP and damage never move sheet stats, so it produces no requirement beyond being printed in the mode's note. The Interact itself is an internal step of the activity, not a lane; only the resulting state matters. The weapon-instance binding is the sharp part: the rider does not attach to a weapon category or to all your Strikes, but to the single wielded weapon coated when the action was taken.

why.numbers: The first two sentences are ancestry flavour. Four mechanical clauses follow. The Nature training and its redundancy fallback are two separate promises — the usual mistake is to record the training and miss the fallback, which is its own lane. The third clause is an action-scoped skill substitution (Sense Direction and Subsist are Survival actions), not a bonus. The fourth constrains a different, later pick rather than changing a number.
why.resources: Four clauses after the flavour opener: a fixed skill training, a redundancy fallback that turns into a free pick, a substitution of Nature for two Survival actions, and a restriction placed on a later draconic-exemplar choice. The last has no lane that genuinely fits — it constrains another record's option list rather than granting or modifying anything — so it is stated as text.

requirements.clause: Choose one of the domains associated with your mystery for which you have an initial domain spell.

This is a category reclassification of a granted spell, not a modifier.

The first is a filtered pick — the option list is not all domains but the intersection of your mystery's domains with those where you already have the initial domain spell, so the filter itself is part of the requirement. The second grants a focus spell whose identity depends on that pick, which is the effectChoices[].grant shape. Judging only from the text: it says nothing about increasing the focus pool, so focusPool is NOT promised here.
why.resources: Two clauses: a filtered pick made when the feat is taken, and a focus spell whose identity depends on that pick. The text says nothing about the focus pool, so no pool increase is required.
why.unmodellable: Three clauses. The choice is not a free list — its options are computed from the character's mystery AND from which initial domain spells they already hold. The grant is a focus spell selected by that choice. The final clause is a rules reclassification, not a number: the granted spell is cast as a REVELATION spell, which puts it under the oracle's revelation/cursebound rules rather than plain focus-spell rules. The printed text says nothing about a focus pool increase, so none is claimed here.

requirements.clause: Select a number of potions equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1); these potions must be of 9th level or lower.
requirements.freeText: A repeated pick whose COUNT is derived from the character's Intelligence modifier with a floor of 1, and whose option list is filtered to potions of level 9 or lower. The text also says the picks can't be changed once chosen, so the stored answers must be treated as fixed rather than re-rollable.

requirements.clause: You gain formulas to create these potions as alchemical consumables with the elixir trait.
requirements.freeText: No lane in the manual covers adding entries to a character's known-formula list. The requirement: each chosen potion must appear among the character's known formulas AND be re-typed there as an alchemical consumable carrying the elixir trait — so that it counts as an elixir everywhere the sheet asks 'is this an elixir', including whatever pools Quick Alchemy and Advanced Alchemy draw from. The re-typing, not just the formula, is the load-bearing half.

requirements.clause: Select a number of potions equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1); these potions must be of 9th level or lower. Once you've chosen the potion formulas, they can't be changed.
requirements.freeText: The player must make a multi-pick whose number of slots equals the character's Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) and grows if that modifier later grows, with the list filtered to potions of 9th level or lower. Once picked, the sheet must treat the entries as locked and not re-openable.

requirements.clause: You gain formulas to create these potions as alchemical consumables with the elixir trait.
requirements.freeText: The chosen potions must join the character's known formulas, recorded as alchemical consumables carrying the elixir trait, so they show up wherever the sheet lets the character make alchemical items — including the daily-preparation alchemy list and Quick Alchemy — rather than only as potions.

requirements.clause: Select a number of potions equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1); these potions must be of 9th level or lower. ... Once you've chosen the potion formulas, they can't be changed.
requirements.freeText: A multi-pick whose NUMBER of selections is computed from the Intelligence modifier with a floor of 1 (so it can move when Int changes), whose option list is filtered to items of the potion category at level 9 or lower, and whose result is locked permanently once made rather than re-chosen on rest.

requirements.clause: You gain formulas to create these potions as alchemical consumables
requirements.freeText: The selected potions must join the character's known formulas so they become producible through Quick Alchemy and the daily advanced-alchemy allotment, i.e. they have to appear in the pools those systems draw from.

requirements.clause: as alchemical consumables with the elixir trait
requirements.freeText: No lane covers this: the feat rewrites the identity of another record. A potion — a magical consumable — must exist on this character's sheet as an ALCHEMICAL consumable carrying the elixir trait, so that everything keyed to alchemical items and to the elixir trait (Quick Alchemy, advanced alchemy, alchemist feats keyed to elixirs) sees it. The sheet needs a way to hold a re-typed variant of an existing item rather than the item itself.

why.numbers: Three clauses, of which two are requirements. The selection clause is unusual in that the NUMBER of picks is derived from a live attribute modifier (Int, minimum 1) and the option list is filtered by item level, and the text explicitly locks the picks once made. The formula clause does two things at once — it adds entries to what the character knows how to make, and it re-types those potions as alchemical consumables with the elixir trait, which is what makes them legal alchemist output. The reagent-for-magical-components and toolkit substitutions are crafting requirements, explicitly not lanes. Nothing here is an ally, enemy, or aura effect.
why.resources: Two clauses that touch the sheet: a locked, Intelligence-sized pick of potions, and those potions becoming known formulas re-typed as elixirs. The reagent-substitution and toolkit clauses are crafting requirements, which are explicitly not requirements. Nothing in the lane list covers gaining formulas, so that clause is stated as text rather than forced into a near-miss lane.
why.unmodellable: Four clauses. The selection clause is unusual twice over — its COUNT is computed from the Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) rather than being a fixed number, and its options are filtered by item category and level. The formula grant feeds the alchemy pool. The re-typing clause is the sharp one: an item printed as a magical potion has to exist on the sheet as an alchemical consumable with the elixir trait, which is a rewrite of another record's own type and traits. The reagent/toolkit substitution is a crafting requirement, explicitly a non-lane, so it yields nothing beyond text. 'Once you've chosen ... they can't be changed' makes the pick permanent rather than a daily one, which is a property of the choice, folded in below.

requirements.clause: you can also choose a skill in which you're already trained
requirements.freeText: The sheet must let the player pick one skill from among the skills they are already trained in, and remember that pick for the duration (the pick is made fresh each time Ancient Memories is used, not fixed at character build).

requirements.clause: and become an expert in that skill
requirements.freeText: Your own proficiency rank in the chosen skill rises trained -> expert, and every number derived from it (the skill modifier, and any DC or check that reads that rank) must move accordingly. Unlike the usual rank-upgrade case this is not a permanent level-keyed step: it is temporary and its target is chosen at use time.

requirements.clause: This lasts until your Ancient Memories expires.
requirements.freeText: A turn-on/turn-off state whose lifetime is borrowed from a different ability (Ancient Memories), carrying the expert rank while running and reverting the skill to trained when it ends.

requirements.clause: When the effects of Ancient Memories and Endless Memories expire, you can retrain one of your skill increases. The skill increase you gain from this retraining must either make you trained in the skill you chose with Ancient Memories or make you an expert in the skill you chose with Endless Memories.
requirements.freeText: Printed permission that after the effects lapse the character may retrain one skill increase, restricted to the two skills that were chosen. The player performs the retrain themselves; the sheet only has to state the permission and its restriction.

requirements.clause: When you choose a skill in which to become trained with Ancient Memories, you can also choose a skill in which you're already trained
requirements.freeText: A second pick offered at daily preparations, alongside the Ancient Memories pick. The player must choose one skill, and the offered set is restricted to skills the character is ALREADY trained in (so the picker's legal options depend on the character's current proficiencies, including the Lore skills they happen to have).

requirements.clause: and become an expert in that skill
requirements.freeText: The chosen skill's proficiency rank must read expert while the pick is live — a rank set driven by a player choice rather than by level, and temporary rather than permanent, so it must not be usable as a prerequisite for a skill increase or any permanent character option.

requirements.clause: This lasts until your Ancient Memories expires.
requirements.freeText: The expert rank's duration is not its own — it is bound to the parent record's pick. Both picks must be made at the same daily preparation and both must clear at the next one, on one shared clock; there is no Endless Memories pick without a live Ancient Memories pick.

requirements.clause: When the effects of Ancient Memories and Endless Memories expire, you can retrain one of your skill increases. The skill increase you gain from this retraining must either make you trained in the skill you chose with Ancient Memories or make you an expert in the skill you chose with Endless Memories.
requirements.freeText: A printed allowance that, once both temporary picks lapse, the player may re-point one of their permanent skill increases — and that the re-pointed increase is limited to the two skills that were chosen. The act is a build edit the player performs; the constraint is prose worth showing, not something computable.

requirements.clause: When you choose a skill in which to become trained with Ancient Memories, you can also choose a skill…
requirements.freeText: This feat has no effect of its own — it edits what another record (Ancient Memories) does when used, turning that feat's one pick into two and hanging a second effect off it. The sheet must be able to attach a rider onto another feat's activation rather than treating this as a standalone grant.

requirements.clause: you can also choose a skill in which you're already trained
requirements.freeText: A player pick made at activation time, whose option list is not a fixed list of names but is computed from the character's own state: only skills in which they are currently trained are eligible.

requirements.clause: and become an expert in that skill. This lasts until your Ancient Memories expires.
requirements.freeText: A temporary state that raises the chosen skill's proficiency RANK one step, trained to expert, for everything that skill feeds (its check, and any DC built from it), and then drops back. Two unusual parts: the thing being changed is a rank rather than a bonus, and the duration is not its own — it must end exactly when the other feat's effect ends.

requirements.clause: When the effects of Ancient Memories and Endless Memories expire, you can retrain one of your skill increases. The skill increase you gain from this retraining must either make you trained in the skill you chose with Ancient Memories or make you an expert in the skill you chose with Endless Memories.
requirements.freeText: The player may go back and reassign one already-spent skill increase, and the replacement pick is legal only if it lands on one of the two skills named during the expired effect. So the sheet needs to (1) let a locked-in skill-increase pick be changed after the fact, outside the normal downtime retraining route, and (2) remember which two skills were chosen while the effect ran, since they define what the new pick is allowed to be. Nothing in the lane list covers a grant that reaches back and rewrites an earlier advancement choice.

why.numbers: The only feat in this range whose effect lands on your own sheet. Split into clauses: (1) when Ancient Memories fires you additionally pick one skill you are ALREADY trained in; (2) that skill becomes expert; (3) the bump lasts exactly as long as Ancient Memories; (4) on expiry you may retrain one skill increase, constrained to the two skills involved. Clauses 1-3 are a real, own-sheet proficiency change — a player-chosen, temporary rank bump living inside another ability's duration. Clause 4 is a rebuild permission the player executes by hand, so it is only worth printing. Nothing here is an ally, enemy, or GM matter.
why.resources: Four separable mechanical clauses. Unlike the rest of this batch, every one of them lands on the character's OWN sheet: an extra pick made at daily preparations, a proficiency rank the pick sets, a duration that has to be shared with the parent record's pick, and a printed retraining allowance. Ancient Memories (the prerequisite) reads 'During your daily preparations, you can explore your memories... to become trained in one skill of your choice. This proficiency lasts until you prepare again.' — so 'until your Ancient Memories expires' means the next daily preparation, not an encounter timer. Nothing here is GM-adjudicated, ally-facing, or an internal activity step.
why.unmodellable: Four separate mechanical promises, and only the first is obvious. (a) It rides on ANOTHER feat's activation, adding a second pick to Ancient Memories. (b) The pick is a player choice constrained to skills you are already trained in. (c) The payload is a temporary proficiency RANK change (trained -> expert) that must expire when Ancient Memories does — a rank moving inside a timed state, not a number. (d) A separate, later clause hands out a constrained retrain of a skill increase. Nothing here lands on an ally, an enemy, or the battlefield, so no DECIDED SCOPE ruling applies.

why.numbers: Every mechanical clause lands on someone else. The benefit (+1 status bonus to saving throws until the end of their next turn) is granted to 'an ally that recovers Hit Points from your Lay on Hands' — in PF2e you are not your own ally, so nothing reaches your own saves. Ruling F/N settles this: an effect on a teammate produces nothing on your sheet, no star and no modifier, because the feat's own description already tells the player what the ally gets. The opening sentence ('create an aura of protection that defends your allies') is flavour, and even read as an aura it is covered by Ruling M. The feat grants no action of your own, no resource, and no change to any of your numbers.
why.resources: One mechanical clause, and it lands entirely on someone else: 'An ally that recovers Hit Points from your Lay on Hands gains a +1 status bonus to their saving throws until the end of their next turn.' The recipient is explicitly an ally, so it is never the character themselves. Under the settled ruling that an effect landing on a teammate produces nothing on your sheet — no star, no modifier, no surface — this feat asks nothing of the character sheet. There is no self-facing clause to salvage: the feat adds no action, no use to spend, no choice to make, and no toggle; it is a permanent, automatic rider on a spell the character already has, whose entire payload is a number on another creature's save.
why.unmodellable: The whole feat is one clause and it lands entirely on someone else: 'An ally that recovers Hit Points from your Lay on Hands gains a +1 status bonus to their saving throws.' Ruling F/N is explicit — an effect on a teammate produces nothing on your sheet, and the record's own description tells the player what the ally gets. Nothing in the text touches the champion's own statistics, and the fact that the rider hangs off your Lay on Hands does not change whose sheet the bonus lands on.

why.numbers: Three separate mechanical clauses, all of them ally-side: the healed ally gets a +1 status bonus to THEIR attack rolls, deals 1 extra spirit damage on THEIR Strikes, and THEIR Strikes gain the holy trait — all until the end of their next turn. Ruling F/N puts every one of them outside your sheet. Your own attack rolls, damage dice, and weapon traits are untouched; the trigger clause (an ally recovering HP from your Lay on Hands) is a trigger, not a requirement. Nothing to express.
why.resources: Three separate mechanical clauses — '+1 status bonus to their attack rolls', 'deals 1 additional spirit damage on all their Strikes', and 'all their Strikes are holy' — but every one of them attaches to the same subject: 'An ally that recovers Hit Points from your Lay on Hands'. All three are teammate-side, and the two damage clauses are additionally about damage, which never moves sheet stats. Nothing is chosen, tracked, or spent by the character: no per-day uses, no toggle, no daily-preparation decision, no new action. Settled scope means the correct amount of sheet surface is zero.
why.unmodellable: Three distinct mechanical clauses — a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, 1 additional spirit damage on Strikes, and the Strikes gaining the holy trait — but all three are worded on the recipient ('An ally that recovers Hit Points… their attack rolls… all their Strikes'), and in PF2e an ally is a creature other than you. Ruling F/N settles all three: an effect landing on a teammate is nothing on your sheet. Note that the third clause would otherwise be interesting (a Strike acquiring a trait is a rules change, not a number) — it is still the ally's Strike, so it stays off this sheet.

why.numbers: One mechanical clause, and it is triply out of scope: the recipient is an ally (Ruling F/N — an effect on a teammate produces nothing on your sheet), the trigger is standing inside your Shield the Faithful emanation (Ruling M — auras are settled, not a missing system), and the payload is 10 temporary Hit Points ('HP and damage never move sheet stats'). The first sentence is flavour. Your own AC, saves, HP, and actions are unchanged.
why.resources: A single clause that is triply covered by settled scope: 'An ally who begins their turn in your Shield the Faithful aura gains 10 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 round.' The recipient is an ally (teammate effects produce nothing on your sheet); the gate is standing inside an emanation (auras are decided, not a missing system); and the payload is temporary Hit Points (HP never moves sheet stats, even inside a mode). The feat also adds nothing to spend or choose — Shield the Faithful's own once-per-hour use and 1-minute duration belong to that record, not to this one, which merely appends an ally-facing rider.
why.unmodellable: One clause, and it is settled three times over. The recipient is an ally, not you (Ruling F/N). The trigger is standing inside your Shield the Faithful emanation, and Ruling M has already decided that positional aura membership is unknowable and is not a missing system. The payload is temporary Hit Points, and Ruling E states that HP and damage never move sheet stats even inside a mode. Nothing is required on the champion's own sheet.

why.numbers: Two clauses. The first — 'when you successfully damage an opponent with either Guiding Shot or Set-Up Strike' — is a trigger line referencing actions you already have from elsewhere; it grants nothing and is explicitly not a requirement. The second gives the fortune effect (roll twice, take the higher) to 'the next creature other than you' attacking that target, i.e. it is worded to exclude you outright, and it also attaches to the enemy target's state. Ally-side and enemy-side both produce nothing on your own sheet. No number of yours changes.
why.resources: The one mechanical clause reads 'the next creature other than you to attack the same target ... rolls twice on their attack roll and takes the higher result' — the beneficiary is expressly excluded from being the character, and the fortune effect lands on another creature's attack roll against an enemy. Both halves are outside the sheet: someone else's roll, and an enemy as the anchor. The trigger clause ('When you successfully damage an opponent with either Guiding Shot or Set-up Strike') is a trigger, not a requirement, and the two named actions are granted by their own feats, not by this one. Nothing is chosen, tracked, or spent: the feat has no uses, no toggle, and grants no new action.
why.unmodellable: The payoff clause explicitly excludes you: 'the next creature other than you to attack the same target… rolls twice on their attack roll and takes the higher result.' Rolling twice and taking the higher is a genuine rules change rather than a number, which is exactly the shape worth hunting — but it happens on another creature's roll, which Ruling F/N puts off your sheet, and the state it creates lives on the enemy target, which the DECIDED SCOPE also excludes. The trigger clause ('successfully damage an opponent with Guiding Shot or Set-Up Strike') is a trigger line and the existence of those actions comes from their own feats, so it asks nothing here either.

why.numbers: A single mechanical clause: 'You don't provide lesser cover to enemies against your allies' attacks.' What it removes is a circumstance bonus to the ENEMY's AC against an ALLY's attack roll — both sides of that are explicitly outside the sheet ('an effect on an ENEMY, or on the battlefield, is not your sheet... the target's AC or cover — none is a requirement', plus Ruling F/N for the ally's roll). None of your own attack, AC, saves, speed, or senses move. The first sentence is flavour.
why.resources: One mechanical clause: 'You don't provide lesser cover to enemies against your allies' attacks.' Although the subject is the character, the quantity it changes is a cover state on an enemy, applied to allies' attack rolls — the enemy's defence side of someone else's roll. Both enemy/battlefield state and teammate-facing bonuses are settled as producing no sheet surface. It moves none of the character's own numbers, is always on rather than a toggle, and involves nothing to choose, track, or spend.
why.unmodellable: 'You don't provide lesser cover to enemies against your allies' attacks' changes a circumstance on the battlefield — specifically the cover an enemy has against someone else's attack. That is named twice in the DECIDED SCOPE: effects on enemies or the battlefield are not your sheet, and the target's cover in particular gets no surface ('this dosent need to have an effect the player will tel the gm'). It alters nothing about your own AC, rolls, or actions, so it needs no field at all.

requirements.clause: This feat serves as the rogue's Mastermind racket for the purpose of meeting prerequisites.
requirements.freeText: The sheet must record that holding this feat satisfies the 'Mastermind racket' prerequisite when eligibility for other records is checked, so that feats and options gated on being a Mastermind rogue become selectable. It must do so WITHOUT conferring the racket itself or any of the racket's own benefits — the counts-as is limited to prerequisite checking.

requirements.clause: This feat serves as the rogue's Mastermind racket for the purpose of meeting prerequisites.
requirements.freeText: The sheet needs a way for one record to satisfy prerequisites written against a DIFFERENT record without granting it - a 'counts as' alias consulted by whatever decides which feats a character is eligible for. Having this feat must make every option gated on the Mastermind racket selectable, while the racket's own benefits are not gained. Nothing in the lane manual expresses an eligibility-only equivalence; grantsClassFeature is the wrong shape because it would hand over the racket itself.

why.numbers: Three mechanical clauses. (1) On a success at Recall Knowledge to identify a creature, that creature becomes off-guard against your attacks until the start of your next turn, and (2) on a critical success it is off-guard for 1 minute. Both land entirely on the ENEMY — off-guard is explicitly named in DECIDED SCOPE as a target-side effect that produces nothing on your own sheet, so neither clause is a requirement. The feat also grants no bonus to the Recall Knowledge check itself, and Recall Knowledge is an existing general skill action, so there is no situational bonus and no grantsAction. (3) The only clause touching your own character state is the counts-as line: the feat serves as the rogue's Mastermind racket for meeting prerequisites. This is a body-text counts-as rule, not the stat block's Prerequisites header, and it changes which other records you qualify for. No lane fits it — grantsClassFeature would over-grant, since the feat gives prerequisite-satisfaction only and not the racket or any of its benefits — so it is stated in freeText.
why.resources: Two mechanical clauses, neither of which asks anything of the character sheet. (1) The off-guard clause places its entire payload on the ENEMY — the creature becomes off-guard against your attacks until the start of your next turn, or for 1 minute on a critical success. DECIDED SCOPE settles this: an effect on an enemy or the battlefield is not your sheet, and off-guard and the target's AC are named explicitly as producing no requirement, no star, and no modifier. The duration is likewise tracked on the target, not on you. Note also that this is not a bonus TO your Recall Knowledge check — it is a consequence of succeeding at one — so Ruling C (star every skill that could perform the action) and Ruling D (attach a valueless bonus to the thing it modifies) do not apply; there is no bonus to attach. The feat grants no action either: Recall Knowledge is a universal action every character already has, and the feat only adds a rider to its outcome. Against the player-facing lens: nothing is chosen when the feat is taken, there are no per-day or per-hour uses, no focus points, no toggle or stance, no daily-preparation decision, and no new action, spell, or feat is gained. (2) 'This feat serves as the rogue's Mastermind racket for the purpose of meeting prerequisites' is a prerequisite-satisfaction clause, which the brief lists among the things that are not requirements. So the record legitimately requires nothing of the sheet.
why.unmodellable: Three clauses. The two off-guard clauses (on a success, until the start of your next turn; on a critical success, for 1 minute) place a condition on the ENEMY, which DECIDED SCOPE settles as producing nothing on your sheet - off-guard and the target's AC are named there directly - so neither the base effect nor the degree-of-success branch is a requirement, and the Recall Knowledge trigger is just a trigger line. The third clause is a genuine mechanical promise with no lane: the feat must count AS a different record (the rogue's Mastermind racket) when OTHER records' prerequisites are evaluated. That is not this feat's own prerequisite (excluded), it is a counts-as alias that changes which other records are reachable, and no lane in the manual covers it - grantsClassFeature would be a near-miss because the racket is not actually gained, only impersonated for eligibility.
